title: Get Ready
excerpt: Every day we face battles we can't fully see. A walkthrough of the full armor of God in Ephesians 6 — what each piece actually protects, and what putting it on deliberately looks like today.

blocks.text: Would a doctor begin an operation without surgical gear? Would a firefighter run into a burning building without a protective suit? Would a soldier head into battle without armor?

With the exclusion of extreme situations, of course they wouldn't. Not only do they spend years preparing for these moments, but they also learn how to protect themselves from harm. Without that preparation, they can't do their job — and the risk isn't hypothetical. It's the whole reason the gear exists.
Writing to the believers in Ephesus from inside a Roman prison, the apostle Paul used the same logic for something far less visible than a fire or an operating table:

verses: Put on all of God's armor so that you will be able to stand firm against all strategies of the devil.

blocks.text: Every day, we face battles we can't fully see — discouragement that shows up out of nowhere, temptation that catches us off guard, doubt that creeps in during a quiet moment. If we're not prepared for that kind of fight, we can't do the job we've actually been called to: loving God and loving people well. God's armor is readily available to every believer. But like any piece of protective gear, it doesn't do us any good sitting in the closet. It has to be put on — deliberately, piece by piece, before the fight is already underway.
So what exactly is this armor, and what does "putting it on" actually look like?
The Belt of Truth

verses: Stand your ground, putting on the belt of truth.

blocks.text: In a Roman soldier's uniform, the belt wasn't decorative — it held everything else together and kept loose clothing from tangling a soldier's legs mid-battle. Truth functions the same way in our lives. Without it, everything else we're wearing starts to shift and slip. Putting on truth means anchoring yourself daily in what God actually says — about who He is, who you are, and what's real — instead of the shifting narratives fear, culture, or your own insecurities hand you. Practically, this looks like returning to Scripture often enough that it becomes your default filter for reality, rather than something you reach for only in a crisis.
The Breastplate of Righteousness

A breastplate covers the vital organs — the heart, specifically. Righteousness here isn't about moral performance; it's the righteousness of Christ, already given to those who belong to Him. Putting on this piece means guarding your heart with the truth of your identity in Christ rather than letting shame, guilt, or the accusations of the enemy find a way in. Practically, this looks like refusing to let condemnation set up camp where Christ has already declared you clean — and letting that security shape how you actually live.
Shoes of the Gospel of Peace

verses: For shoes, put on the peace that comes from the Good News.

blocks.text: Roman soldiers wore sandals fitted with spikes for stability and traction on uneven ground. The gospel does something similar — it gives us solid footing no matter what terrain we're standing on. Putting on this piece means walking into your day already secure in the peace Christ has made with you, instead of scrambling to find peace in your circumstances. Practically, this looks like carrying that peace into hard conversations, uncertain seasons, and relationships — becoming someone whose steadiness comes from somewhere deeper than the moment.
The Shield of Faith

verses: In addition to all of these, hold up the shield of faith to stop the fiery arrows of the devil.

blocks.text: Roman shields were large enough to block an entire body, and soldiers often locked them together with the shields of the people fighting beside them. Faith works the same way — it's not passive belief, it's an active shield raised against the specific lies and doubts aimed at you. Putting on this piece means choosing, in the moment a fiery thought lands — "you're not enough, God's forgotten you, this will never change" — to raise what you know to be true about God against it. Practically, this looks like naming those "arrows" out loud and answering them with Scripture rather than letting them sink in unchallenged, and staying close to other believers who can lock shields with you when your arms get tired.
The Helmet of Salvation

verses: Put on salvation as your helmet.

blocks.text: A helmet protects the mind — and few things are more contested in spiritual warfare than the mind. The certainty of your salvation is what guards your thoughts from despair, comparison, and the lie that your standing with God is ever in question. Putting on this piece means regularly reminding yourself that your salvation isn't fragile or performance-based; it's secure. Practically, this looks like taking captive the thoughts that try to make you forget that (2 Corinthians 10:5), and refusing to let your mind camp out in places that contradict who God says you are.
The Sword of the Spirit

verses: ...and take the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.

blocks.text: Every other piece of this armor is defensive. This one isn't. The Word of God is the one weapon we're given to actually push back against the enemy — the same weapon Jesus used against temptation in the wilderness, answering every lie with Scripture instead of argument (Matthew 4:1-11). Putting on this piece means knowing God's Word well enough that it's ready in your hand when you need it, not something you have to go searching for mid-battle. Practically, this looks like committing key verses to memory and letting them become your first response to temptation, rather than your last resort.
Getting Dressed on Purpose

None of this armor puts itself on. That's the part easy to miss in Paul's instructions — every verb is active. Put on. Stand firm. Hold up. Take. This isn't gear God straps onto us while we're asleep. It's a daily, deliberate decision to dress ourselves for a fight that's already happening, whether we've suited up for it or not.

So before the day gets away from you, consider actually walking through this — truth around your waist, righteousness over your heart, peace under your feet, faith in your hand, salvation on your head, and the Word ready as your weapon. It is a real preparation of someone who knows the battle is real and doesn't intend to walk into it unarmed.

God, You have equipped me with tools that draw me closer to You, and help me to stand against the schemes of the enemy. Thank You for Your protection. Thank You for always looking out for me. Today, help me to intentionally put on all of the armor You freely offer me. Give me the strength to stand firm in You. In Jesus' name, Amen.
